name: Pregabalin

tolerance.full: within several months of continuous use

toxicities: Common label-reported effects include dizziness, somnolence, dry mouth, peripheral edema, blurred vision, weight gain, and difficulty with concentration or attention.
Serious risks include life-threatening respiratory depression with CNS depressants or respiratory impairment, angioedema with respiratory compromise, and suicidal thoughts or behavior.
Abrupt or rapid discontinuation may increase seizure frequency and cause withdrawal symptoms; suicidal behavior or ideation has also been reported after discontinuation.
summary: Pregabalin (Lyrica) is a GABA derivative that is used to treat neuropathic pain and seizures, as well as anxiety.
metabolism: Undergoes negligible how the body breaks it down. Elimination is primarily renal as unchanged pregabalin, so CYP breakdown does not explain its how fast the body clears it.
generalRisks: The DailyMed label warns that pregabalin may cause serious, life-threatening, or fatal respiratory depression with CNS depressants, including opioids, or with underlying respiratory impairment. Other warnings include dizziness and somnolence with driving impairment, angioedema/hypersensitivity, suicidal thoughts or behavior, edema and weight gain, and increased seizure frequency or withdrawal symptoms after abrupt cessation.
saferUse: Avoid driving or hazardous machinery until the effect on alertness and coordination is known.
Use caution with opioids or other CNS depressants and respiratory impairment; seek immediate care for slowed breathing or swelling of the face, mouth, tongue, or throat.
Do not stop suddenly; the label advises gradual tapering over at least one week. Monitor for mood changes or suicidal thoughts, including after discontinuation.
